issues.legal_issue: A proprietor whose land was recorded as khud-kasht before statutory vesting may retain possession of it even though it was subject to a mortgage with possession and the mortgagor had surrendered possession to the mortgagee.
material_facts: The plaintiffs were proprietors of the suit lands and had mortgaged them with possession.
The lands were recorded as the plaintiffs’ khud-kasht in the annual village papers before vesting.
The first appellate court found that the plaintiffs had cultivated the lands before the mortgage.
The statutory vesting converted the mortgage with possession into a simple mortgage, and the plaintiffs sought possession as well as redemption.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiffs were entitled to possession under Section 4(2), and the High Court’s refusal of possession was reversed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 3 and 4(1)(a) of the Madhya Bharat Zamindari Abolition Act, proprietary rights vested in the State; Section 4(1)(f) converted an existing mortgage with possession into a simple mortgage. Notwithstanding those consequences, Section 4(2) allowed a proprietor to remain in possession of khud-kasht land recorded as such in the annual village papers before vesting. Khud-kasht includes land cultivated by the proprietor personally or through employees or hired labourers. The Court relied on its earlier decision in this litigation, which had remitted the case for determination of the khud-kasht issue.

rule.if: appeal_in_redemption_and_possession_suit and proprietor_of_land and land_cultivated_by_proprietor_or_workers and land_recorded_as_khud_kasht_before_vesting

predicates.appeal_in_redemption_and_possession_suit: A party appealed in a suit seeking redemption of a mortgage and possession of the land.
predicates.proprietor_of_land: The claimant held proprietary rights in the land before those rights vested in the State.
predicates.land_cultivated_by_proprietor_or_workers: The proprietor cultivated the land personally or through employees or hired labourers.
predicates.land_recorded_as_khud_kasht_before_vesti: The land was recorded as the proprietor’s khud-kasht in the annual village papers before vesting.

issues.definition: When a proprietor appeals in a redemption-and-possession suit and the land was cultivated by the proprietor or workers and recorded as khud-kasht before vesting, the proprietor is entitled to retain possession.

issues.legal_issue: Tenants placed on mortgaged land by a mortgagee in possession must yield possession on redemption unless an intervening law gives them an independent right to remain.
material_facts: The land was mortgaged with possession.
The evidence supported a finding that the mortgagors cultivated the land before the mortgage and that the mortgagee’s relatives later cultivated it.
Even assuming the mortgagee inducted tenants, the Court found no statutory right that entitled those tenants to remain in possession against the proprietors’ claim under the land-reform law.
issues.conclusion: Any tenants inducted by the mortgagee had no right to remain in possession on redemption in this case and could not defeat the proprietors’ claim to possession.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 76(a) and (e) of the Transfer of Property Act, a mortgagee in possession must manage the property as a prudent person and must not act destructively or injuriously; a lease granted by the mortgagee ordinarily cannot extend beyond the mortgage and ends on redemption. Mahabir Gope v. Harbans Narain Singh established that rule and its exception for rights conferred on tenants by statute. The Court also relied on Harihar Prasad Singh v. Mst. of Munshi Nath Prasad, Asa Ram v. Mst. Ram Kali, and Prabhu v. Ramdev, which applied or reiterated those principles. Here, the land-reform law protected the proprietors’ possession, and no statutory tenancy right was established for the tenants.

predicates.mortgage_redemption_proceeding: The proceeding concerns redemption of a mortgage over land.
predicates.tenants_placed_on_land_by_mortgagee: The mortgagee in possession placed tenants on the mortgaged land.
predicates.tenants_have_independent_statutory_right: A law confers on the tenants a right to remain on the land independently of the mortgagee’s interest.

issues.definition: When a mortgage is being redeemed, tenants placed on the land by the mortgagee must yield possession unless they have an independent statutory right to remain.
